# E025 -- Channel 4

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Channel 4
- **Industry:** Broadcasting / Television
- **Year:** Not dated (estimated mid-2000s based on references to QuarkXPress and "new identity")
- **Region:** United Kingdom
- **Source file:** c4styleguide1-1-pdf.pdf
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 3-5, 6-7, 12-25

## Brand Strategy
- Brand values: innovative, independent, irreverent.
- The identity is about "transformation and movement" -- the original animating logo embodied an organisation constantly re-inventing itself and challenging viewer expectations.
- "The new Channel 4 identity uses cutting edge technology to push the brand into exciting new areas."
- Off air (print/collateral) and on air (broadcast) identities treated as distinct but unified systems.

## Logo
- In print, the logo facia is invisible -- only its distinctive shadow is seen, overlaying photographs, illustrations, and textures.
- The logo "always foregrounds the real stars of the channel -- the shows."
- Logo continuously changes: adapts texture and colour to its surrounding environment.
- **Distinctive placement:** Centre-right position (not bottom-right like most brands) -- described as "unique to the channel and instantly recognisable."
- Minimum size: 10mm height (print), 30px deep (web). No maximum size.
- Colour: may be taken from the image it's placed over, or may be black or white.
- Isolation area and misuse rules defined.

## Typography
- **Bespoke typeface:** C4 -- "the first bespoke typeface in Channel 4's history."
- OpenType format, supported on PC and Mac.
- **Weights:**
  - C4 Headline Regular: for large titles and posters, effective at 14pt+. Only weight placed in text boxes. Type in boxes always upper and lower case.
  - C4 Text Regular: light, clean, practical body copy font. Best at 7, 9, 10, 11, 12pt.
  - C4 Text Bold: for emphasis in small titles, headings, sub-headings.
  - C4 Medium: heavier than Regular, effective for longer text at 14pt+.
  - C4 Condensed: for on-screen or off-air when large text must fit small space. Regular, italic, bold, bold italic.
  - C4 Guides: used specifically to make text boxes.
  - All weights have corresponding italics.
- **Leading formulas:**
  - Headline: font size x 1.1 (auto leading 10% in QuarkXpress).
  - Body copy: font size x 1.2 (auto leading 20% in QuarkXpress).
- Minimum type size: 5pt. No maximum.

## Color
- Logo colour is adaptive -- can be taken from underlying imagery, or default to black/white.
- No fixed corporate colour palette specified in sampled pages; the brand identity is designed to be chameleon-like.

## Graphics / Illustration
- The logo shadow effect is the primary graphic device -- the "4" shape appears as a shadow over any content.
- No standalone illustration system described; programme imagery is the visual hero.

## Photography
- Programme imagery is central -- "the logo always foregrounds the real stars of the channel -- the shows."
- Imagery is described in the advertising section, with poster and press layout guidance.

## Applications
- **Print/poster advertising:** Four key outdoor formats and six press formats.
- **Literature:** Logo position, height, margins defined for collateral.
- **Stationery:** Letters, envelopes specified.
- **Sub-brands:** Separate section for Channel 4 family brands.
- **Programme support and consumer products** also covered.
- Sponsorship and third-party logo rules; response advertising; black-and-white reproduction rules.

## Tone of Voice
- Explicitly defined: "bold, surprising and challenging" -- matching the brand values of innovative, independent, irreverent.
- "Sound bites work well on posters and in advertising. They keep communication clear and simple."
- Example headlines demonstrate sharp, provocative copywriting:
  - "Drug companies are making a killing" (Dying for Drugs)
  - "Nigella sucks" (Nigella Bites)
  - "Skin to die for" (Six Feet Under)
  - "Magic is dead" (Derren Brown)
  - "View, vote, control" (Big Brother)
- **Detailed editorial style guide:**
  - "four" in Channel 4 always as numeral.
  - Lowercase web, email, voicemail, job titles.
  - Prefer "and" over "&".
  - No full stops in acronyms; specific hyphen/en-dash/em-dash rules.
  - Numbers 1-10 written out; 11+ as figures.
  - Italics instead of quotation marks for programme/book/film titles.

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- The transparent/shadow logo concept is highly unusual -- the logo has no visible face, only its shadow exists in print applications.
- Centre-right logo placement as a deliberate brand differentiator from the universal bottom-right convention.
- Bespoke typeface with a dedicated "Guides" weight specifically for creating text boxes is an uncommon level of font tooling.
- The leading formulas (font size x multiplier) provide a mathematical approach rather than fixed values.
- Very detailed editorial style guide integrated into visual identity guidelines -- covering punctuation, number formatting, decade styling, and technical terminology.

## Quality Score
4 / 5 -- Comprehensive identity system with a distinctive conceptual foundation (shadow logo, adaptive colour, centre-right placement). The bespoke C4 typeface family is well documented with practical sizing guidance. The tone of voice section with real campaign examples is strong. Loses a point for lack of formal colour palette specifications and limited photography direction beyond programme imagery.
